evidence.title: Bolt: Supported browsers; Mobile
evidence.finding: Bolt works in Chromium desktop browsers and Safari. Phone browsers support prompting, preview, publishing, sharing and restore; Code view, visual edits and database tools are desktop-only. Home-screen installation is web access, not evidence of a native phone app.

evidence.title: Bolt: Agents
evidence.finding: Bolt offers Standard and paid Max agents and selects their models internally. This is not evidence of Claude Code or other named external harness support.

evidence.title: Bolt: Billing
evidence.finding: Bolt subscriptions provide token allocations for builder usage; Free use refreshes daily and monthly and paid allocations follow the billing cycle.

evidence.title: Bolt: Ways to start a project; Bolt and StackBlitz
evidence.locator: Ways to start a project; Bolt and StackBlitz
evidence.finding: Users start with prompts, Figma, Stitch, GitHub or a Lovable import. WebContainers provide a browser Node.js development environment without local installation.

evidence.title: Bolt: Connect to an MCP server
evidence.finding: Users can connect built-in connectors such as Notion, Linear and GitHub, or a custom MCP server, so Bolt can read and interact with external tools and data.

evidence.title: Bolt: Ways to start a project
evidence.finding: A natural-language prompt creates a project; GitHub and design imports bring an existing starting point. No persistent native issue tracker is established by this flow.

evidence.title: Bolt: Plan before building
evidence.finding: Plan Mode lets users discuss an approach before code changes, then switch to building after refining scope.

evidence.title: Bolt: Project knowledge
evidence.finding: Project settings store project knowledge for the agent, separate from a single chat prompt.

evidence.title: Bolt: Search; Reference files
evidence.finding: Code view permits browsing files and paths for references in prompts. Safari makes these files read-only and disables file search.

evidence.title: Bolt: Work together in real time
evidence.finding: A Bolt project has one shared chat and processes one prompt at a time; prompts sent during generation are queued. This explicitly limits one shared project, not all projects on an account.

evidence.title: Bolt: Work together in real time
evidence.finding: Bolt queues later prompts from collaborators until the current project prompt completes.

evidence.title: Bolt: Queue prompts
evidence.finding: Chat tools let users queue follow-up prompts while Bolt is busy and manage the queued requests.

evidence.title: Bolt: Intro to Bolt
evidence.finding: Users can build and refine with natural-language chat, change agent choice and optionally edit source directly.

evidence.title: Bolt: Bolt and StackBlitz
evidence.finding: The development environment runs on WebContainers, which run Node.js in the browser. Hosted Bolt Cloud deployment is a separate output-service scope.

evidence.title: Bolt: Safari
evidence.finding: Safari previews are hosted rather than running in the browser and must be regenerated after changes. This does not prove laptop-independent agent execution.

evidence.title: Bolt: Branching and merging
evidence.finding: Bolt can create and switch GitHub branches and keeps branch-specific memory. A branch is not a documented worktree or hostile-code security sandbox.

evidence.title: Bolt: Version history
evidence.finding: Built-in version history lets users restore earlier project versions. No server crash or process reconnection test was performed.

evidence.title: Bolt: Use the terminal
evidence.finding: Chromium Code view exposes a terminal to run project commands; Safari does not expose the terminal. Automatic dependency, port and cache reliability remains untested.

evidence.title: Bolt: What is included in the Free plan
evidence.locator: What is included in the Free plan
evidence.finding: Free use has daily and monthly limits. Free hosting caps are ten GB bandwidth and 333,333 monthly requests; a site exceeding them goes offline for the rest of the month. These are hosting limits, not agent-runtime timeouts.

evidence.title: Bolt: Check your sync status
evidence.finding: The GitHub panel shows Syncing or Synced status, linked repository and active branch. A GitHub conflict message offers pull-and-resend or pull-and-discard choices.

evidence.title: Bolt: Tokens
evidence.finding: Builder usage is measured in tokens and visible in account usage. Model-provider invoices and per-task marginal charges were not reconciled.

evidence.title: Bolt: Work together in real time
evidence.finding: Shared-project prompts run serially and excess prompts queue. This does not establish compute-aware global concurrency scheduling.

evidence.title: Bolt: Work together in real time
evidence.finding: Collaborators prompt and edit the same project in one shared chat. Bolt processes one prompt at a time; tokens come from the person prompting.

evidence.title: Bolt: Team member roles
evidence.finding: Team Admins manage membership, roles, billing, project controls and integrations; Members build within those controls. The owner has Admin permissions.

evidence.title: Bolt: Share integrations
evidence.finding: Only the project owner manages the GitHub connection. Collaborator edits sync when the owner next opens the project, and only the owner can connect or prompt MCP connectors.

evidence.title: Bolt: Version history
evidence.finding: Project version history and restore preserve prior code states. This is not evidence of an immutable audit log with a retention guarantee.

evidence.title: Bolt: Add comments to your project and send them to Bolt
evidence.locator: Add comments to your project and send them to Bolt
evidence.finding: Users can leave threaded feedback on preview elements. Editors and co-owners send selected comments to Bolt as instructions. These are preview comments, not an established code-diff review UI.

evidence.title: Bolt: Work together in real time; Share integrations
evidence.locator: Work together in real time; Share integrations
evidence.finding: Collaborators share a single chat and project, while GitHub sync waits for the original project owner to return. Full runtime takeover after owner disconnect remains unverified.

evidence.title: Bolt: Intro to Bolt
evidence.finding: Bolt exposes a live app preview and source through Code view. A persistent cross-task reviewer-output gallery was not found in the checked pages.

evidence.title: Bolt: Security audit
evidence.finding: Users can run a project security audit (paid plans) or a database security check (all plans), review the findings and have Bolt fix them; a check before publishing is recommended. The source does not establish enforced mandatory checks or independent review.

evidence.title: Bolt: Branching and merging; GitHub sync
evidence.finding: Bolt creates and switches branches and automatically syncs project changes to GitHub. The guide recommends opening PRs in GitHub; it does not establish native PR creation inside Bolt. Merging branches in-app is explicitly unsupported.

evidence.title: Bolt: Change branches in Bolt
evidence.finding: Bolt does not currently merge branches in-app; users merge through GitHub. This restriction is scoped to the Bolt interface.

evidence.title: Bolt: Project and Site
evidence.finding: Publish creates a hosted site and later project edits require another explicit Publish update to reach the live site.

evidence.title: Bolt: Backups, restore and version history
evidence.finding: Users can restore prior project versions and export project backups. Restore does not establish stale approval invalidation.

evidence.title: Bolt: Export your project
evidence.finding: Project code can be downloaded as a backup and synced to GitHub. App code export does not establish self-hosting of the core Bolt service or full chat history portability.

evidence.title: Bolt: Billing; Monthly plan example
evidence.finding: The documentation gives a USD 25 monthly Pro 10M example and monthly or annual billing, with token allocations and separate hosting limits. The live plan selector is authoritative for current paid tiers.

evidence.title: Bolt: October 26 to November 1
evidence.finding: Release notes document database tables becoming private by default starting October 30 and expanded phone browser workflows in October. No shutdown notice was identified.

evidence.title: Bolt: What is included in the Free plan
evidence.locator: What is included in the Free plan
evidence.finding: The ongoing Free plan supports build, publish, viewer/editor/co-owner project sharing and recurring daily/monthly use. Custom domains are excluded and published sites retain Made in Bolt branding.

evidence.title: Bolt: Billing; Cancel your subscription
evidence.finding: Plans disclose token allocation, monthly or annual billing and a downgrade to Free when paid cancellation takes effect. Public task-level monetary cost is not fixed.

evidence.title: Choose an agent
evidence.locator: Agent choices; Standard; Max; Forge note
evidence.finding: The picker offers Standard and Max, with Forge for eligible accounts. Bolt controls model selection; the complete picker does not offer external coding-agent harnesses.

evidence.title: Bolt pricing
evidence.locator: Free, Pro, Teams and Enterprise; monthly billing
evidence.finding: The full plan list offers Free, Pro at USD 25 per month, Teams at USD 30 per member per month and custom Enterprise. Plans meter token allowances. Enterprise includes SSO. No API-key, one-time license or per-machine ADE plan appears.

evidence.title: StackBlitz terms of service
evidence.finding: The terms expressly include hosted Bolt and grant a non-exclusive, non-transferable access license. They restrict reverse engineering, modification and redistribution of the service. The open-source starting repository is outside this hosted-service scope.

evidence.title: Account settings
evidence.finding: A Model training switch controls use of projects and chats for training. It is not documented as a switch disabling product telemetry.
